The agreement opens an entirely new advertiser category for the company and reshapes how travelers encounter protection options during planning and booking.

The addition reflects the accelerating expansion of Expedia Group Advertising beyond its traditional base of hotels, airlines, and destinations. Over the past year, the business has increasingly powered campaigns for non-travel brands, from retail to entertainment to financial services, connecting them with high-intent traveler audiences across Expedia Group's sites and apps, offsite channels, and partner publishers. Redion's arrival extends that trajectory into travel insurance and assistance, a category that sits at the intersection of both worlds.

The two companies are not new to each other. For more than 15 years, Redion, formerly known as Europ Assistance worldwide and Generali Global Assistance (GGA) in the U.S., has provided travel protection to Expedia Group customers. This collaboration moves that relationship beyond product distribution into a strategic advertising alliance, with co-branded editorial, on-platform experiences, and targeted activations rolling out across Expedia Group brands beginning in Q3 2026.

For travelers, the shift means that Redion can now cohesively appear throughout the traveler's journey to maximize brand awareness and peace of mind.

Expedia Group's research points to the opportunity: 62% of travelers made a non-travel purchase tied to their most recent major leisure trip, spending an average of $500 beyond the trip itself, and 38% of Gen Z travelers bought financial products or services before departure. For Redion, that creates a timely opportunity to reach travelers as they consider trip-related protection and financial decisions.

"Opening a category is not something we do often," said Jennifer Andre, Vice President, Business Development at Expedia Group. "Redion earned this as our first insurance advertising partner because of a 15-year track record of protecting our travelers. Together we can bring travel protection into the journey earlier and more easily than either of us could alone."

"This partnership marks a defining moment for Redion," said Virginie Babinet, CEO, Travel Insurance & Assistance – Redion Group. "As we introduce the Redion brand to the world, we're doing it from the center of the traveler's journey, alongside a longstanding partner. We intend to make it a partnership that others are measured against."

releases.title: IAB Releases Measurement Services Addendum v1.0 for Public Comment
releases.body:
New Draft Framework Introduces Standardized Contractual Terms for Advertising Measurement, Verification, Attribution, and Analytics Services

Public Comment Open Until October 22, 2026

NEW YORK, Sept. 22, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Interactive Advertising Bureau (IAB), the leading trade association for the digital advertising industry, today released the Measurement Services Addendum v1.0 for public comment, introducing a standardized contractual framework for companies that provide, purchase, or use advertising measurement, verification, attribution, and analytics services. Developed through IAB's Terms & Conditions Task Force, the addendum expands IAB's modular legal framework to support more consistent, efficient, and interoperable agreements across the digital advertising ecosystem. The public comment period will be open for 30 days until October 22, 2026.

"Reliable measurement is fundamental to a healthy digital advertising marketplace, but the legal frameworks supporting those relationships have often been shaped one agreement at a time," said David Cohen, CEO, IAB. "By developing a common contractual foundation for measurement services, we're giving the industry a practical starting point that can reduce friction, improve efficiency, and help organizations spend less time negotiating custom agreements and more time delivering value for all."

The Measurement Services Addendum is the latest component of IAB's modular legal framework, building on the General Terms v1.1 and Direct Buy Addendum v1.0 released earlier this year. Designed for use by advertisers, agencies, publishers, media owners, platforms, and measurement providers, the framework establishes standardized terms for advertising measurement relationships, helping reduce contractual fragmentation, streamline negotiations, improve operational efficiency, and create greater consistency across the digital advertising ecosystem while remaining flexible enough to accommodate different technologies, methodologies, and business models.

"Measurement has become increasingly sophisticated, but the contracts governing those services haven't kept pace," said Cintia Gabilan, SVP, Centers of Excellence & Industry Initiatives, IAB. "The Measurement Services Addendum gives organizations a practical legal framework they can adopt as written or incorporate into existing agreements, making it easier to create greater consistency across measurement relationships while accommodating different business models and technologies."

The public comment package includes the Measurement Services Addendum v1.0, General Terms v1.1 and Appendix 1 – Definitions v1.1, which together establish a shared legal baseline for advertising measurement relationships. The General Terms are incorporated by reference into the addendum and are intended for use with an applicable addendum rather than as a standalone agreement.

IAB invites advertisers, agencies, publishers, platforms, measurement providers, ad technology companies, and legal, procurement, finance, privacy and ad operations professionals to review the draft and provide feedback. Comments received during the public comment period will be considered in the finalization process.

Public comments will be accepted through October 22, 2026. Feedback, including suggested edits, implementation questions, and general usability comments, may be submitted to terms-comments@iab.com. Draft documents are available here.

About IAB

The Interactive Advertising Bureau (IAB) empowers the media and marketing industries to thrive in the digital economy. Its membership comprises more than 700 leading media companies, brands, agencies, and the technology firms responsible for selling, delivering, and optimizing digital ad marketing campaigns. The trade group fields critical research on interactive advertising, while also educating brands, agencies, and the wider business community on the importance of digital marketing. In affiliation with the IAB Tech Lab, IAB develops technical standards and solutions. IAB is committed to professional development and elevating the knowledge, skills, expertise, and collaboration of the workforce across the industry. Through the work of its public policy office in Washington, D.C., the trade association advocates for its members and promotes the value of the interactive advertising industry to legislators and policymakers. Founded in 1996, IAB is headquartered in New York City.

FORT WORTH, Texas, Sept. 22, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Simpli.fi, the real-world media platform built for the age of immediacy, has launched Simpli.Hub, an on-demand self-serve advertising portal that balances corporate brand control with local execution, allowing multi-location brands, franchise networks, co-ops, and distributed agencies to create consistent yet localized ads across various markets and channels, from programmatic to walled gardens.

However, scaling localized campaigns for even as few as three locations, let alone hundreds, creates operational bottlenecks, brand drift, and fragmented reporting. Adding to the challenge, many local operators or store managers have limited advertising experience, leading to unnecessary time spent trying to localize an ad or funneling precious ad dollars to the wrong channels. In most cases, corporate either struggles to micromanage ad spend or is left to trust operators with limited experience to know how to best use that spend. It's a lose-lose situation that wastes time and money for all involved.

"Multi-location advertisers have historically had to choose between strict brand control and local flexibility," said Michael Schoen, Chief Product and Technology Officer of Simpli.fi. "Simpli.Hub delivers both. By bridging corporate strategy and local execution, teams can unlock unused local ad budgets and convert them into store foot traffic, helping to direct every location to reach the target customer at the right moment while avoiding wasted spend."

Built on top of the Simpli.fi unified media platform as an easy-to-use storefront for multi-location execution, Simpli.Hub empowers local operators and franchise owners with on-demand, self-serve campaign execution without sacrificing top-level brand control or consolidated reporting. Simpli.Hub allows customers to place orders that flow into the Simpli.fi platform for activation across channels from search and display to premium CTV and DOOH, allowing teams to launch fast while maintaining strong corporate alignment. By directly linking digital campaigns to real-world impact, Simpli.fi provides a uniquely scalable solution for distributed teams.

Simpli.Hub turns localized advertising into an efficient, turnkey process:

  • Corporate Control: Corporate teams set the campaign strategy, creative assets, geographic parameters and brand guardrails centrally within the platform.
  • Local Activation: Local franchise operators and store managers select from pre-approved campaign options, set their local budget and launch targeted campaigns across channels without requiring media buying expertise.
  • Unified Intelligence: Corporate leadership gains comprehensive, aggregated visibility into performance across every location, designed to help maximize ad spend effectiveness and drive real-world outcomes.

"Simpli.Hub solved a franchise marketing problem we've been working around for years," said Roxane Harris, Vice President, Franchise Operations & International, H&R Block. "Our operators launch their own campaigns, corporate stays in the loop across every location, and our brand stays consistent—locally relevant, nationally on-brand."

Simpli.Hub connects localized campaigns directly into Simpli.fi's core media capabilities, leveraging place-based, purchase and identity signals to link digital engagement with real-world store visits.

Simpli.Hub is available starting today, following successful rollouts with multi-location brands and enterprise franchise networks managing campaign activations across thousands of locations nationwide.

NEW YORK, Sept. 22, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Today, IAB Tech Lab, the global digital advertising technical standards-setting body, announced AAMP 3.0, the next major release of its Agentic Advertising Management Protocols framework, introducing a standardized way for buyers and sellers to move from an RFP through proposal evaluation and toward a buy commitment in agentic advertising.
releases.title: IAB Tech Lab Introduces AAMP 3.0 to Standardize the RFP-to-Buy Process for Agentic Advertising
releases.body:
OpenProposal Brings a Common Standard to a Historically Manual Stage of Media Buying, Connecting RFPs to Buy Commitments and will be in Public Comment until October 22, 2026

NEW YORK, Sept. 22, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Today, IAB Tech Lab, the global digital advertising technical standards-setting body, announced AAMP 3.0, the next major release of its Agentic Advertising Management Protocols framework, introducing a standardized way for buyers and sellers to move from an RFP through proposal evaluation and toward a buy commitment in agentic advertising.

While standards exist for many stages of digital media buying and execution, the process between an RFP and a buy commitment has historically been handled largely through human and manual workflows. As AI agents take on more responsibility for discovering, evaluating and planning media, that gap creates the need for a common way for buyer and seller agents to exchange and evaluate proposals before a transaction moves toward execution.

AAMP 3.0 addresses that gap through OpenProposal, a new specification that defines how sellers can represent advertising products and respond to buyer briefs in a standardized, agent-readable format. OpenProposal enables buying agents to discover and compare opportunities against a brief while giving sellers control over how their inventory and ad products are represented. The new specification will be in Public Comment until October 22, 2026, during which time it will be built into the Buyer and Seller Agent SDK reference implementations.

OpenProposal extends AAMP into the RFP and proposal stage while connecting to the IAB Tech Lab standards already used across media execution, including AdCOM, OpenDirect, and the Deals API. Together, these standards provide a common foundation for agentic workflows to move from discovery and planning through negotiation, buying, execution and reporting.

"As agents take on more of the work in media planning and buying,the industry needs a common framework for the RFP and proposal process," said Anthony Katsur, CEO, IAB Tech Lab. "OpenProposal fills a major gap between a buyer's brief and a buy commitment, giving buyer and seller agents a standardized way to exchange and evaluate opportunities. By connecting that process to the standards the industry already uses for execution, AAMP 3.0 creates a foundation for agentic workflows across the media buying lifecycle."

From Discovery to Execution

OpenProposal creates a standard way for publishers to define advertising products and packages and to represent them in RFP responses. Buying agents can evaluate those proposals against a buyer's brief, compare opportunities and assess suitability before moving toward a buy commitment. Once an opportunity moves forward, AAMP connects that proposal to the standards and infrastructure used for all types of transaction and execution.

AAMP 3.0 supports a media lifecycle that includes:

  • Publish: Sellers publish a catalog of public packages that can be browsed, while retaining some products for custom proposals.
  • Discover: Buyer agents retrieve available public packages, enabling inventory discovery before a negotiation begins, or submit a full brief to get a custom proposal.
  • Compare: Buyer agents evaluate and rank opportunities against a declared brief, creating the ability to process information from a broader set of publishers than would be practical through manual evaluation alone.
  • Qualify: Agents evaluate availability and fit for the specific audience, flight and requirements of a media plan.
  • Negotiate: When needed, buyer and seller agents can negotiate custom terms while maintaining a reference to the original published offer.
  • Bind & Execute: Transactions can be executed using the existing standards and infrastructure of the digital advertising ecosystem.
  • Report: Performance can flow back through existing reporting standards, allowing results to be evaluated against the original objectives and commitments of the plan.

AdCOM provides a common vocabulary throughout these stages, allowing the information represented at discovery to remain consistent as an opportunity moves through planning, negotiation, execution and reporting.

OpenProposal Makes Publisher Ad Products Agent-Readable

OpenProposal gives publishers a standardized way to make a broader range of ad products understandable to buying agents and to create proposals in response to buyer briefs. In the proposal, sellers can include information necessary for buyers to understand how the products can be bought, executed, measured and evaluated.

For buyers, this creates the ability to evaluate a much broader universe of potential media opportunities. Agentic technology can process and compare more information across more publishers than a human planner could reasonably evaluate alone, helping buying organizations build plans informed by a larger and more diverse consideration set.

OpenProposal maintains continuity with the digital advertising infrastructure already in the market. It complements OpenDirect, AdCOM, and the Deals API, using those established standards as opportunities move from planning into transaction and execution. Existing programmatic implementations of those standards can continue operating as they do today, without requiring DSPs, SSPs or other technologies to change their existing use cases.

In addition, the AAMP agent software development kits (SDKs) continue to further harden deterministic guardrails governing pricing, ad packages, orders and media buy details, increase trust in agent identities, and strengthen idempotency across transactions to help ensure consistent responses and data integrity as agents operate at greater speed and scale. In practical terms, idempotency means an instruction can be sent twice without happening twice; so when an agent retries a request it didn't get an answer to, the result is confirmation of the original order rather than a duplicate.

Industry Support for an Agentic Media Ecosystem

As agencies, brands and publishers begin building agents into their planning and transaction workflows, industry participants are rallying around the need for common standards that allow those agents to communicate across companies and platforms. AAMP agents with OpenProposal are designed to create that shared foundation while allowing every participant to maintain control over its own technology, inventory, business rules and data.

"By providing full agentic coverage for all existing IAB Tech Lab standards, while at the same time standardizing agent authentication and authorization protocols, AAMP 3.0 delivers a transaction-ready framework that will aid our industry's movement from proof-of-concept tests towards the wide-spread use of AI Agents in media transactions." added Michael Palmer, Global Vice President, Emerging Technologies at WPP Media.

"Agentic planning gives us the opportunity to evaluate a much broader range of media opportunities and information when we build a plan," added Mike Treon, Head of CTV Strategy at PMG. "What's new in AAMP 3.0 is that the reasoning travels with the proposal. A seller can tell us not just what a package costs, but why they believe it fits the brief — the audience rationale, the formats, the terms behind the price. That context is what our planning models need, and now it arrives in a form they can actually read."

The global IAB Network is also getting involved. "IAB Australia has opened expressions of interest for a seller-side pilot using the AAMP reference implementations available today," said Jonas Jaanimagi, Technology Lead, IAB Australia. "We've been running those implementations in a lab for months and contributing feedback upstream. Our role now is to help Australian publishers test discovery, proposal and approval workflows in a sandbox before any live spend is involved, and to turn that practical experience into useful evidence for the industry."

AAMP 3.0 represents the next stage in IAB Tech Lab's work to apply agentic capabilities to the proven standards that underpin digital advertising. By standardizing the RFP-to-buy commitment process and connecting it with established standards for transaction, execution and reporting, AAMP 3.0 helps create a common foundation for agentic media buying without requiring the industry to rebuild the infrastructure it relies on today.

To review the OpenProposal specification, supporting technical resources, and to provide feedback, via Public Comment until October 22, 2026. please visit: iabtechlab.com/AAMPv3.

About IAB Technology Laboratory

Established in 2014, the IAB Technology Laboratory (Tech Lab) is a non-profit consortium that engages a member community globally to develop foundational technology and standards that enable growth and trust in the digital media ecosystem. Comprised of digital publishers, ad technology firms, agencies, brands, and other member companies, IAB Tech Lab focuses on solutions for brand safety and ad fraud; identity, data, and consumer privacy; cross-channel programmatic effectiveness and ad measurement; and the impact of LLMs and AI agents on advertising. Its work includes the OpenRTB real-time bidding protocol, ads.txt anti-fraud specification, Open Measurement SDK for viewability and verification, VAST video specification, Trusted Server, and the Agentic Roadmap initiative for agentic advertising. Board members and companies are listed at https://iabtechlab.com/about-the-iab-tech-lab/tech-lab-leadership/. For more information, please visit https://iabtechlab.com.

AUSTIN, Texas, Sept. 21, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Status Labs, the premier digital reputation management firm in The Millbrook Companies agency collective, is pleased to announce its No. 10 ranking on the 2026 Advertising & Marketing Agencies list by the Austin Business Journal.

Status Labs was founded in Austin in 2012, at a time when online reputation management had yet to become an established industry. Fourteen years later, the firm remains headquartered in Austin while serving enterprise organizations, growth-stage businesses, family offices, and high-profile public figures in over a dozen countries through satellite offices in New York, Los Angeles, Miami, and London.

Its gradual expansion to new markets – and continued growth in the Austin market where the company and the Millbrook holdco originated –  can be attributed to a commitment to cutting-edge innovation, which most recently has been exemplified by Status Labs early entry and expertise in the burgeoning generative engine optimization vertical. 

The firm has built its business around a question that has become central to modern corporate reputation: What do people find – and now, what are they told – when they seek information about an organization or individual?

That question has taken on new urgency with generative AI. AI platforms such as ChatGPT, Gemini, and Perplexity increasingly provide direct answers rather than a page of links, shaping how customers, investors, partners, journalists, and the public encounter a company for the first time.

Status Labs formally launched its Generative Engine Optimization, or GEO, offering in October 2025. The work itself began earlier, as the firm studied how emerging generative AI systems were interpreting, synthesizing, and recommending information about companies and public figures in 2023, before GEO was widely recognized as a service category.

Today, GEO is Status Labs' fastest-growing workstream, accounting for almost a quarter of new client engagements in the first half of 2026.

"Status Labs was built on the understanding that reputations are increasingly formed online, often before a client has the opportunity to tell its own story," said Darius Fisher, CEO of Millbrook Companies and co-founder of Status Labs. "As AI becomes a primary interface for information, that work has become more consequential. The question is no longer only where a company ranks in search. It is whether the answer someone receives accurately reflects who that company is."

Status Labs' 2026 AI Reputation Report found that roughly 60% of searches now end without a click to a website. When AI systems assemble an answer, the report found, they draw heavily on earned media and other third-party sources—not simply the material a company publishes about itself. Visitors who arrive through an AI-generated answer convert at 4.4 times the rate of visitors from organic search.

For clients operating across markets, sectors, and public audiences, the consequence is practical: a company can have a strong website and a well-defined brand, yet still be inaccurately represented—or absent entirely—when an AI platform is asked who leads its category.

Status Labs' GEO practice combines AI-driven language-model diagnostics, semantic content mapping, and credibility-signal engineering. The firm audits how large language models interpret and summarize a client's business; structures priority messages so they remain intact through AI summarization; and strengthens the high-quality, corroborating sources that influence whether a model cites a company, represents it accurately, or overlooks it altogether.

"A decade ago, a reputation challenge often appeared as a page of search results," Fisher said. "Today, it may appear as a paragraph response assembled from sources a company did not create. We began preparing for that shift before there was a standard name for the work because the direction of the internet was already clear."

Status Labs is part of Millbrook Companies, which brings together earned media, owned content, search, and reputation strategy through Status Labs, Sensei Advisory, and BLP.

The 2026 Advertising Agencies list is available via ABJ. To request a GEO consultation, visit StatusLabs.com/Contact.

About Status Labs

Status Labs is the world's leading digital reputation management, SEO, and generative engine optimization (GEO) firm for Fortune 500 companies, growth-stage businesses, family offices, and public figures. Founded in 2012 and headquartered in Austin, Texas, Status Labs is now part of Millbrook Companies alongside agencies Sensei Advisory and BLP. To learn more about Status Labs, visit StatusLabs.com.

releases.body:
Study finds growing AI adoption, confidence and governance across advertisers and agencies

NEW YORK, Sept. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The Advertising Research Foundation (ARF) today released a new research report, How Marketers Are Using Artificial Intelligence, examining how advertisers and agencies are adopting AI across marketing, media, research and measurement. The study finds that AI is now widely used for creative development, media buying, customer engagement, analytics, campaign measurement, synthetic data and AI-generated personas.

Business, advertising and marketing industry publications.

Confidence is rising alongside adoption. Among marketers using AI, average confidence in AI-generated outputs increased from 82% in November 2025 to 93% in May 2026. At the same time, organizations are becoming more systematic about AI: extensive testing reached 64%, and formal training programs grew from 50% to 70% between the two survey waves.

"AI is becoming embedded in how marketers work, from creative development to analytics and measurement," said Scott McDonald, Ph.D., President and CEO of the ARF. "As adoption accelerates, the industry needs to put the same energy into validation, governance and standards, so marketers can understand when and how these tools can be trusted."

The study finds that there is no single dominant AI system across marketing functions. Instead, adoption varies by use case, with platform-native tools playing a major role in media buying and measurement, while different providers lead in creative, analytics and other applications.

The study also finds that marketers see immediate benefits from AI in efficiency and speed, higher-quality insights and improved targeting, while data privacy, inaccurate outputs and brand safety remain leading concerns. Overall, the findings point to an industry where adoption and confidence are advancing quickly, but shared standards and validation practices are still developing.

Read the full report, How Marketers Are Using Artificial Intelligence, at thearf.org.

About the ARF

Founded in 1936 (over 90 years ago), the Advertising Research Foundation (ARF) is the leading organization dedicated to creating better advertising through research, standards and collaboration. With more than 400 member companies, the ARF advances the science and practice of advertising, media and marketing.

releases.body:
New Concession Will Modernize Airport Media Network and Support Long-Term Growth Strategy

PENSACOLA, Fla., Sept. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Clear Channel Outdoor's Airports Division, the leading U.S. airport sponsorship and advertising partner, today announced it has been selected to manage the advertising concession at Pensacola International Airport (PNS). The agreement gives Clear Channel Outdoor (CCO) responsibility for delivering a refreshed airport media program that connects brands with more than 3.1 million annual passengers and strengthens the airport's position as a key commercial gateway for the Gulf Coast region.

Following a competitive selection process, PNS selected CCO to lead its advertising program, which has been managed in-house since 2018. Having previously served as the airport advertising concessionaire until 2012, CCO will return with a major investment in upgraded infrastructure and new sponsorship inventory. The program is designed to modernize the terminal environment, enhance revenue opportunities, and introduce more dynamic, technology-enabled advertising formats across high-traffic passenger areas.

"Pensacola International Airport is experiencing remarkable growth, and we're proud to partner with the airport at such a pivotal moment in its development," said Morten Gotterup, President, Clear Channel Outdoor Airports Division. "This agreement enables us to bring a new level of innovation to the airport environment, creating high-impact opportunities for brands to engage travelers through modern, technology-driven media while enhancing the overall experience for the millions of passengers who move through PNS each year."

PNS is the busiest airport along the Interstate 10 corridor between Jacksonville and New Orleans, serving a broad mix of business, leisure, and military travelers. The airport offers 28 nonstop destinations and is served by major carriers including American, Delta, United, Southwest, Breeze, Frontier, and Contour.

Modernizing the Passenger Environment

The new advertising program aligns with PNS's broader capital investment strategy, including a $165 million terminal expansion and new concourse scheduled for completion in the first half of 2028, which will add five gates to the existing 12-gate facility.

"Pensacola International Airport is in the midst of one of the most transformative periods in our history, and every investment we make should reflect the future we're building," said Matt Coughlin, Executive Director of Pensacola International Airport. "Clear Channel Outdoor shares that vision by bringing innovative, technology-driven advertising solutions that will elevate the passenger experience while creating meaningful opportunities for businesses to connect with millions of travelers each year. We're excited to partner with them as we continue shaping the next chapter for PNS."

CCO's Airports Division will introduce a modernized advertising program across key passenger touchpoints, including:

  • Branded LED video walls across entryways, security checkpoints, and baggage claim – Large-format digital displays placed at key passenger touchpoints, delivering high-impact brand storytelling throughout the airport journey.
  • Digital concourse advertising network – A connected network of screens throughout the concourse, reaching travelers as they move between gates, dining, and retail areas.

The campaign follows one family across three generations in the same home, celebrating the central role the home played in a family's life in a letter drafted to wish the new owner well. 

As the Coldwell Banker® brand celebrates its 120th anniversary this year, the campaign honors all of the little moments that add up to make a house into a home: the dinner parties, holiday celebrations, graduations, visitors, and new additions. The 60-second spot tells one family's story across more than 30 years, while a series of original 15-second spots highlight individual moments in the family's life – and the home that served as the setting. It's a vantage point Coldwell Banker has held since 1906, across generations of families and the agents who walked them through the door.

"The Letter isn't about the value of a house in dollars, cents or square footage. It's about the value of life that happens inside," said Brandon Newman, Vice President of Marketing, Coldwell Banker Real Estate LLC. "Homes are an ecosystem for your life, so we built our campaign the same way. There is no single hero spot with cut downs. Instead, there's a whole life that takes place in this world we have created, which celebrates the real lives people live in their homes every day." 

Capturing three decades of one family in the same home shaped every production choice, from casting to cameras. The Coldwell Banker team cast the family at multiple ages, spent up to six hours a day on makeup to age or de-age actors, and evolved wardrobe and production design through the decades. Three cameras marked the passage of time, including a 16mm film camera for the earliest era.

"Much of the conversation around real estate today is about technology, listings, transactions and market conditions, but buying or selling a home has always been about more than that," said Mary Lee Blaylock, President of Coldwell Banker Affiliates. "Homes are incredibly emotional, and after 120 years in the business, Coldwell Banker has seen all of it. Coldwell Banker affiliated agents don't just close transactions. They hand people the keys to the places where their lives unfold. Times Square Media Companies Join 9/11 Day for Unprecedented 9:11 A.M. Tribute

NEW YORK, Sept. 10, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- On the morning of September 11, 2026, many of Times Square's iconic digital billboards will pause their normal advertising to participate in a special National Moment of Silence at 9:11 a.m. ET, marking the 25th anniversary of the September 11 attacks.

The first-of-its-kind observance is being organized by the nonprofit 9/11 Day, with support from the Times Square Alliance and The Broadway League, along with support and participation from leading companies in the out-of-home advertising industry.

At 9:11 a.m., more than 30 participating Times Square displays will simultaneously feature a commemorative message during a one-minute Moment of Silence. Immediately afterward, singer Francesca "Ces" Picerno, who lost her father, Matthew Martin Picerno, in the terrorist attacks of 9/11, will join young performers from Broadway Bound Kids for a live rendition of "America the Beautiful."

9/11 Day Calls on Americans to "UNIITE For Good."

At the Moment of Silence observance, in Duffy Square, 9/11 Day will also unveil a 40-foot-long fully lit sculpture entitled "UNIITE." The sculpture, which was on display in Central Park on September 9, and at the Intrepid Museum on September 10, is part of 9/11 Day's nationwide 25th anniversary activities, encouraging Americans to remember and honor the victims of 9/11 and those who rose in service by joining together in unity and doing good deeds in their communities. For more information about how to pledge a good deed, visit 911day.org .

The Moment of Silence tribute has special personal meaning for Jay Winuk, who co-founded 9/11 Day in 2002 with his friend, David Paine. Jay's younger brother Glenn, an attorney and longtime volunteer firefighter and EMT, was killed in the line of duty in the collapse of the World Trade Center South Tower.

"As did so many first responders, my brother Glenn ran toward danger that morning to help people he didn't know, to serve his community," said Winuk, executive vice president of 9/11 Day. "Twenty-five years later, these few minutes of silence observed in the heart of Times Square is a simple but deeply meaningful act of remembrance for those we lost. I'm enormously grateful to the many participating companies and advertisers for making this possible."

"Our goal is to create a National Moment of Silence in America when our nation can take a moment to pause in remembrance of the 9/11 tragedy, and those impacted by it," said David Paine, co-founder and president of 9/11 Day. "We hope this will become an annual ritual over time."

9/11 Day's marketing partners, Innocean and David&Goliath, have led the way in securing the donated billboard commitments.

Among the media companies supporting the Times Square observance include (partial list as of the date of this news release): BIG Outdoor, Branded Cities, Clear Channel Outdoor, Del Mastro Outdoor, Dream Outdoor, Firefly, Heritage Outdoor, Intersection, KEVANI, Light Year Media,, New Tradition, Orange Barrel Media, OUTFRONT, Paramount, and Silvercast Media.

"Our industry has a unique ability to bring people together in shared public spaces," said Les Harrison of OUTFRONT Media, a leading IRL media company.  "On September 11, these physical screens can serve an even greater purpose — creating a moment when millions of people can pause together, remember and honor those whose lives were forever changed by 9/11."

About 9/11 Day

9/11 Day, a nonprofit, created and annually organizes the federally recognized September 11 National Day of Service and Remembrance. Founded in 2002 by David Paine and Jay Winuk, 9/11 Day works to transform the anniversary of 9/11 into a national day of doing good in tribute to those killed and injured in the attacks, and the many who rose in service in response. www.911day.org.

releases.body:
As AI Reshapes How Consumers Discover and Choose Brands, Advertisers Prioritize Customer Acquisition, Brand Equity and Visibility in AI-driven Discovery

NEW YORK, Sept. 10, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Interactive Advertising Bureau (IAB), the leading trade organization for the digital advertising ecosystem, today released its 2026 Outlook Study: September Update, raising its full-year U.S. ad spend growth forecast to 12.3%, up 2.8 percentage points from its January projection of 9.5%.

Based on insights from more than 200 brand and agency ad investment decision-makers, the updated forecast follows a stronger-than-expected first half fueled by major cyclical events, including the Winter Olympics and FIFA World Cup, along with easing buyer concerns about macroeconomic headwinds. The study also finds marketers prioritizing customer acquisition and brand equity as consumers become more discerning and AI transforms how people discover, evaluate, and choose brands.

"The first half was strong, major live events delivered, and advertisers have increasingly powerful tools in their arsenal to find and engage customers," said David Cohen, CEO, IAB. "At the same time, the economy has real areas of uncertainty. There is growth to be found, but there are no easy wins. When consumers are considering their next purchase, the brands that win will be connecting with them at the right time, in the right context, and with a compelling message."

Marketers Shift Their Focus to Winning New Customers

The updated outlook shows a clear shift in what advertisers want their media investments to accomplish. Customer acquisition, although usually the top media investment goal, jumped nine percentage points since January to 63%, while brand equity rose six points to 43%. Meanwhile, repeat purchases held essentially flat at 24%, after nearly doubling as a priority since 2024.

The change comes as consumers face persistent inflation and cautious sentiment, making shoppers more selective about where their money goes and more willing to switch brands and retailers. For advertisers, that creates both a need to reinforce brand strength and an opportunity to win undecided customers.

"Consumers are becoming more discerning. They're switching brands, paying for lower-priced brands and looking at store brands," said Chris Bruderle, Vice President, Industry Insights & Content Strategy, IAB. "For brands, that means two things. They need to make sure their brand equity is strong, particularly in AI environments. And if people are more willing to switch brands, there's an opportunity to acquire new customers."

Marketers Concerned About LLM Discovery and AI Slop

Marketers are increasingly focused on the consumer using AI platforms and what that means for discovery, consideration, and purchase.

Adapting to evolving consumer behavior, including AI-driven search, is now the top media investment challenge, cited by 44% of buyers. Concern about low-quality AI-generated content, or "AI slop," follows at 38%.

At the same time, optimizing content for AI-generated answers is now the No. 1 area of increased focus among buyers at 76%, followed by AI LLM models at 72%. Focus on generative AI use in media campaigns stands at 69%, compared with 78% in January.

"What we are seeing is a pretty meaningful evolution in the AI conversation," said Brudele. "Marketers have spent a lot of time asking, 'How can I use AI?' Now the question is becoming, 'How do I reach a consumer who uses AI?' People are discovering products and evaluating brands inside these environments. Marketers want to understand how their brands show up in those conversations and how that activity connects to everything else they know about the customer journey."

AI Is Changing the Consumer Journey Faster Than Marketers Can Measure It

That shift is creating a major measurement challenge, with 86% of buyers already changing, or expecting to change, how they measure media performance because of conversational AI tools and AI agents in the next 12 months.

The most common response, selected by 48% of buyers, is measuring brand visibility and citations directly within AI tools. Others are using branded search and direct traffic as proxies, adding third-party AI discovery analysis tools, monitoring AI-platform interactions and referrals, and increasing incrementality testing.

Yet buyers still struggle to connect those signals into a complete view of performance, with 45% citing the difficulty of comparing AI-driven and traditional customer journeys as their top measurement challenge.

"There are important conversations about brands and products happening inside AI environments every day, and marketers are still building the visibility they need into that journey," said Bruderle. "They know the consumer is there. They know these experiences can influence a purchase. Now they are figuring out how to connect those interactions to the signals and outcomes they have measured for years."

A New Playbook for Winning Attention

As audiences fragment across traditional search, conversational AI, commerce platforms, social media, and other discovery environments, advertisers are also changing how they reach consumers. The ad types receiving the most increased focus are:

  • Creator and influencer advertising/partnerships: 54%
  • Demo-targeted and cohort-based advertising: 53%
  • Publishers with first-party data: 48%
  • Contextual advertising: 45%

Together, those priorities point to a broader effort to build trust, identify valuable audiences, and stay visible as consumer discovery becomes more fragmented.

"The pieces really do connect," said Bruderle. "If consumers are moving across more places to discover products, marketers have to think differently about how they earn trust, how they identify the right audiences, and how their content gets found. Visibility is becoming part of the media strategy in a much broader way. It includes the creator someone trusts, the environment where an ad appears, and increasingly what an AI platform says when someone asks about your category or your brand."

The study surveyed 2,200 consumers who have used AI for shopping-related research in the past three months, spanning the U.S., U.K., Australia, Mexico and India.

The findings reveal a clear opportunity for AI platforms to bring trusted creator perspectives into the shopping experience. More than half of consumers (56%) prefer AI-generated shopping recommendations that incorporate creator or influencer perspectives, while 65% say they are more confident in AI recommendations when those recommendations are informed by credible creator reviews.

"AI is reshaping how consumers discover and evaluate products, but as these tools become a more influential part of the shopping journey, trust will be a critical differentiator," said David Cohen, CEO, IAB. "Creator perspectives can help strengthen confidence in AI-generated recommendations by bringing credible human voices into the experience. That's an important opportunity for the industry to embrace as AI continues to reshape commerce."

Younger Consumers Are Leading the Shift

The appetite for creator-informed AI is particularly strong among younger generations. About 65% of Gen Z and Millennials prefer AI recommendations that incorporate creator perspectives, compared with 53% of Gen X and 34% of Boomers. Among Gen Z, creator reviews incorporated into AI recommendations are nearly as influential as brand or advertiser information, at 27% versus 29% respectively.

Creators are also increasingly being discovered through AI itself. Half of Gen Z and Millennials have discovered creators through AI, and nearly three in four say creator-backed recommendations increase their confidence in AI shopping advice.

Authenticity and Expertise Matter More Than Popularity

Consumers are not simply looking for AI to surface the biggest names. The research finds that authenticity and expertise are key drivers of creator trust.

The most trusted creator types are:

  • Everyday consumers (52%)
  • Professional reviewers (43%)
  • Subject-matter experts (37%)

The top factors that make a creator trustworthy enough for AI to rely on their content are:

  • Credibility (46%)
  • Consistency (40%)
  • Expertise (36%)
  • Independence from brands/sponsorship transparency (34%)

"What we're seeing is that with AI shopping, consumers don't just want the recommendation. They want real-world experience and expertise behind the guidance," said Jack Koch, SVP, Research & Insights at IAB. "Our research shows that trusted creator perspectives can increase confidence in AI-generated recommendations, creating an opportunity for platforms to bring more authentic human expertise into the shopping experience."

AI Is Already an Established Part of the Shopping Journey

Eighty percent of consumers are comfortable relying on AI recommendations, creating new opportunities for creator content to play a role throughout the shopping journey. Consumers see the greatest value in creator-informed AI recommendations when finding the best value (38%), discovering products (32%), comparing options (31%) and summarizing product information (31%).

Creator-Informed AI Resonates Across Markets

The value consumers place on credible, authentic creator content is evident across the five markets studied, signaling a global opportunity to bring more human experience into AI shopping recommendations.

Among consumers who have used AI tools for shopping research in the past three months, those in India and Mexico place the greatest value on creator-informed shopping experiences. Compared with consumers in the U.S., U.K., and Australia, they are more likely to want creator perspectives incorporated into AI recommendations and to view creator content as a valuable input to shopping guidance. Among Western markets, the U.S. is the most creator-receptive, while the U.K. is generally the most cautious.

Across all markets, however, the foundation of creator value is consistent: expertise, authenticity, and real-world product experience.

These global shifts in AI-assisted shopping and creator influence will be among the themes explored at IAB's inaugural CreatorFronts, part of IAB Global Creator Week, bringing together platforms, creators, agencies and marketers to examine the future of creator-driven marketing.

About the Research

The IAB Insights Engine study, powered by Attest, was conducted in May 2026 among 2,200 consumers who had used an AI tool for shopping-related research in the previous three months. The study included 1,000 respondents in the U.S. and 300 respondents each in the U.K., Australia, Mexico and India.

At the heart of it all, a central digital hub will bring the world together, curating global event listings, breakthrough insights, and forward-thinking resources from IABs everywhere. releases.title: Storiad Introduces the Author Marketing OS
releases.body:
New software category gives authors a unified system to plan, execute and manage book marketing

CHARLESTON, S.C., Sept. 4, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Storiad today introduced the Author Marketing OS, a new category of software designed to give authors a single system for planning, executing and managing the marketing of their books.

Authors have never had more tools available to market their books. They have social media platforms, email services, advertising platforms, AI tools, websites, databases and countless other resources. Yet those tools remain largely disconnected, leaving authors to figure out how to organize the entire job of marketing a book themselves.

Storiad's premise is simple: authors don't need more marketing tools. They need a system for using them.

"Authors are expected to market their books like businesses, but they've never really had that kind of software businesses use to manage their marketing," said Ramzi S. Hajj, founder of Storiad. "We've had writing software. We've had publishing software. We've had thousands of individual marketing tools. What we've been missing is an operating system for the whole job of marketing a book."

A New Category for an Old Problem

Marketing a book involves far more than creating a few social media posts or sending emails to a limited list.

Authors need to identify their target readers, establish marketing goals, develop a strategy, create promotional materials, find relevant media and industry contacts, conduct outreach, follow up, maintain visibility and measure what is working.

Those activities have traditionally been handled across multiple tools, documents and services.

Storiad brings them together in a single platform designed specifically around the author's book marketing workflow.

The company defines an Author Marketing OS as "a unified system that organizes the major functions of book marketing, including strategy, planning, execution and optimization." Rather than replacing every marketing tool an author may use, the Storiad OS provides the strategic and operational structure that connects those activities.

Storiad is introducing the Author Marketing OS as a new software category built specifically around the job of marketing a book.

From Strategy to Execution

At the center of Storiad's approach is Book Promotion nMotion™, a proprietary system that helps authors turn a book marketing strategy into an actionable campaign.

Book Promotion nMotion™ organizes promotion around eight core areas:

  • Promotional Asset Creation
  • Market Research
  • Social Media Management
  • Emailing & Follow-up
  • Networking
  • Marketing
  • Publicity
  • Blogging & Newsletter

For each area, authors can develop strategies, planning documents and step-by-step checklists designed to move their campaigns from ideas to action.

"There's a really big difference between giving an author a marketing plan and giving an author a system they can actually use to run the campaign," said Hajj. "Our goal is to make book marketing something an author can learn, organize, execute and improve upon over time."

Built Around the Author's Book Sales Goal

Storiad begins with a simple question for the author:

How many books do you want to sell?

Its Book Sales Calculator helps authors establish a specific sales target and understand the marketing activities required to pursue it. From there, the platform provides tools and workflows for building and managing a campaign around that book sales goal.

The platform includes CRM-style contact management, a database of more than 52,000 verified book promotion contacts, marketing planning tools such as a Target Reader Profile, email outreach, social media tools, an author website builder, a press room, publicity resources, campaign management and other book marketing capabilities.

Storiad is being used by thousands of authors, giving the company real-time experience developing software around the practical challenges authors face when promoting their books.

AI as Part of the Marketing System

The Author Marketing OS also incorporates StoriA, Storiad's AI Author Assistant.

StoriA is designed to help authors work through the marketing process, from developing strategies and plans to creating marketing materials and determining what to do next.

"AI is very good at creating things," said Hajj. "But creating another piece of content isn't necessarily the answer to an author's marketing problem. The bigger questions center around who should I reach, what should I say, what should I do next, and how does this fit into my overall campaign? That's where we think AI can become much more useful to authors."

Building the Author Marketing OS

The need for an Author Marketing OS comes from a simple reality of today's publishing environment: authors are increasingly responsible for marketing their own books.

At the same time, the number of tools available to them continues to grow.

Storiad believes the answer is not another standalone marketing tool.

It is a system.

"The ultimate goal is pretty simple," said Hajj. "We want to help authors take control of their book marketing and sell more books."

Storiad is making its Author Marketing OS available to authors through its software platform.

For more information, visit www.storiad.com.

Storiad is the first Author Marketing Operating System, designed to help published authors plan, execute and manage their entire book marketing lifecycle in one place. The platform combines marketing strategy, structured workflows, AI-powered assistance, CRM-style contact management, research, outreach and campaign execution.

Storiad's mission is simple: help authors sell more books.

The acronym, short for "Demand The Limits is Down To Fight", shares the firm's commitment to client service in a bold, unexpected way.

This new campaign embraces self-aware humor in a more modern fashion while remaining grounded in the firm's mission of advocating for injured clients across Florida. Instead of asking viewers to sit through yet another commercial, the goal is to create an advertisement people talk about, share, and remember.

"We know this approach isn't what people expect from us, or a law firm at all for that matter," said Andrew Odza, Co-Founder of Demand The Limits. "That's intentional. Legal advertising has spent decades sounding and doing the same expected advertising.

We believe you can maintain a balance of both professionalism and credibility while doing something different and entertaining."

To further push the concept, DTL is building a broader digital campaign surrounding the wrapped buses. Supporting social content across Meta platforms, TikTok and YouTube strategically welcomes the conversation and provides the Demand The Limits team the ability to see how the public receives and reacts to the campaign in real time.

The campaign reflects a broader shift in how brands are connecting with consumers. As audiences resonate more and more with unconventional advertising, DTL believes the legal industry has the opportunity to join the trend.

The achievement reflects the company's continued investment in building the infrastructure that connects creators, brands, creative strategy, paid media, and performance data into a unified customer acquisition system.

Instead, many companies are shifting toward larger creator ecosystems that continuously test new content, audiences, and messaging before scaling the strongest performers.

The company's proprietary Creator Marketplace plays a central role in that process. Instead of manually recruiting creators for every campaign, brands gain access to a structured marketplace that matches products with creators based on category, audience, demographics, creator style, and historical performance. The marketplace also streamlines contracting, content production, usage rights, creator whitelisting, approvals, and reporting, helping brands launch campaigns more efficiently.

Beyond creator scale, Influencer Advantage emphasizes what it calls meaningful creative diversity. Those insights become increasingly valuable as campaigns grow. The company analyzes billions of creator, campaign, and performance data points to identify patterns that help determine which creators, creative concepts, messages, and audience combinations are most likely to succeed. The objective is not to replace human creativity but to strengthen decision-making through measurable performance data.

"Real people create the content," James Gray added. "Our data helps us understand why it works, so every campaign contributes to stronger performance in the future."

Influencer Advantage's operating model also reflects broader changes taking place across digital advertising. As paid media platforms continue to automate audience targeting, creative quality and authentic creator content have become increasingly important drivers of campaign performance. Brands are placing greater emphasis on testing diverse creator partnerships and amplifying the highest-performing content rather than relying solely on organic reach or follower counts.

The company's integrated approach allows brands to move from creator discovery to campaign activation in less time while maintaining continuous testing and optimization throughout the customer acquisition process. By connecting marketplace activity, creative production, paid media, and performance analysis, Influencer Advantage helps organizations build repeatable systems for long-term growth rather than isolated marketing campaigns.

As creator-led commerce continues to evolve, the company expects brands to invest more heavily in scalable creator ecosystems supported by measurable performance data. releases.body:
Requests DOT Provide Actual Evidence Justifying the Change

WASHINGTON, Aug. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- FlyersRights submitted comments to the U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) in response to its Notice of Proposed Rulemaking titled "Enhancing Flexibility of Air Fare Price Advertising." The proposed rule seeks to either weaken or potentially repeal the 1984 Full Fare Advertising Rule and its 2011 amendments.

The Full Fare Rule, enacted during the Reagan Administration, requires airline advertisements to include the entire price to be paid by a passenger to the airline for a ticket, including taxes and fees. The 1984 rule and the 2011 update were issued in response to complaints of deceptive practices in airfare advertising.

In its public comments, FlyersRights opposed the proposed rulemaking, arguing that the evidence and arguments that the DOT put forward support the status quo or enhanced transparency of all other fees, including optional ancillary fees.

"The same DOT that recently killed the rule to increase transparency in ancillary fees now argues that passengers need transparency into the existence and amount of federal taxes and fees in air travel," explained Paul Hudson, President of FlyersRights. "Airlines already display these taxes and fees prominently, yet with the exception of Southwest Airlines, want to now be able to list them as prominently as, or even more prominently than, the total price."

"This proposed rule is a license for airlines to confuse, deceive, and make it more difficult for passengers to price shop," said Paul Hudson, President of FlyersRights. "Passengers need transparency in the prices on which airlines actually compete–airfare and ancillary fees–not on the mandatory taxes and federal fees that airlines do not control. The DOT, in arguing that airlines need the flexibility to display taxes and fees as prominently as the total price, would be harming passengers, competition, and the airlines that do not wish to deceive their passengers."

FlyersRights has been a long-time advocate for policies that prioritize competition, transparency, and consumer protections within the airline industry.

NEW YORK, Aug. 28, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- As artificial intelligence rapidly changes how marketing work gets done, the Association of National Advertisers (ANA) is calling on the industry to put down the day-to-day work for one day and focus on building the skills marketers will need next.

On Thursday, September 17, 2026, the ANA will host its annual Global Day of Learning, a full day of live master classes, workshops, and conversations built around this year's theme, "The Future of Marketing Work."

The initiative is driven by the ANA Global CMO Growth Council and organized around priorities identified by marketing leaders from around the world.

"AI isn't simply giving marketers another set of tools. It's forcing us to reconsider what skills matter, where human judgment creates the most value, and how the marketing organization itself needs to evolve," said Nick Primola, Group Executive Vice President at the ANA and leader of the Global CMO Growth Council. "Global Day of Learning is our opportunity to collectively push pause on the work immediately in front of us and power up for what's coming next. The goal isn't to predict the future of marketing. It's to give marketers practical ways to prepare for it."

Why is the ANA asking marketers to "push pause"?

Global Day of Learning is built around what the ANA calls "PTO — Personal Time ON": dedicated time to step away from immediate deadlines and focus on learning and skill-building.

This year's "Push Pause and Power Up" call to action reflects the ANA's belief that keeping pace with AI and other industry changes requires marketers to invest in their own capabilities, not just new technology.

Who is speaking at the 2026 ANA Global Day of Learning?

Featured speakers and sessions include:

  • Raja Rajamannar, former Chief Marketing and Communications Officer at Mastercard, on the emerging era of "Quantum Marketing."
  • Shenan Reed, Global Chief Media Officer at General Motors, on the future of cross-media measurement as audiences and media investment fragment across platforms and AI-driven channels.
  • Julia Goldin, Chief Product and Marketing Officer at The LEGO Group.
  • Rahul Chopra, Vice President at Duolingo, and Eric Fulwiler, Co-Founder and CEO of Rival, on building challenger brands at scale.
  • Jennifer Chase, Chief Marketing Officer and Executive Vice President at SAS, on AI, technology, and B2B brand growth.
  • Soyoung Kang, President of eos Products, and creator and entrepreneur Funmi Monet, on the evolution of creator marketing from transactional endorsements toward deeper brand-creator co-creation.
  • Rishad Tobaccowala, Co-Founder of The Athena Project, on future-proofing marketer relevance.

The program will also include hands-on AI training from Cord Silverstein, CEO of IntegrateAI, who will teach participants to build and deploy Custom GPTs and AI agents using ChatGPT, Claude, Copilot and Gemini.

What is the ANA Global Day of Learning?

The ANA Global Day of Learning is an annual industry-wide initiative designed to give marketing professionals dedicated time for education, professional development, and skills-building.

Over the past three years, more than 20,000 marketing professionals and students from more than 100 countries have participated, learning from senior marketers and subject matter experts from across the industry.

The program is a cornerstone of the ANA's investment in developing the marketing profession and is aligned with the ANA Industry Growth Agenda and the priorities identified by the ANA Global CMO Growth Council.

In recent years, the Dinner has featured fireside chats with such notable Newsmakers as Chuck Todd (former host of Meet the Press), Jessica Tarlov (The Five), Alyssa Farah Griffin (The View, CNN), Katty Kay (BBC), Mark Bezos, and Frank Luntz. The Global Summit stage has previously hosted leaders from Colgate-Palmolive, General Motors, Mastercard, McDonald's, PepsiCo, Kroger, Danone, Warner Bros., Paramount+, H&R Block, WPP, Dentsu, Omnicom and many others.

For more information, or to register to attend the Global Summit – part of Out of Home Week New York – please visit www.dpaasummit.com/global.
